create.ponder.track_placement.text_1: Train tracks are a dedicated kind of rail, built for train contraptions
create.ponder.track_placement.text_2: To lay a long row at once, first click the end of a track that is already there
create.ponder.track_placement.text_3: ...then click a second spot, or another track, to fill the gap between them
create.ponder.track_placement.text_4: Connections are not limited to straight lines: they can bend and climb as well
create.ponder.track_placement.text_5: Without help, the connection makes both halves of a turn the same size
create.ponder.track_placement.text_6: Keep the sprint key held while making the connection...
create.ponder.track_placement.text_7: ...and the widest curve that fits between the two ends is used instead
create.ponder.track_placement.text_8: Blocks held in the off-hand get laid beneath new tracks automatically
create.ponder.track_portal.text_1: Lay a track so that it runs straight into a nether portal...
create.ponder.track_portal.text_2: ...and it will try to build a matching track at the portal on the other side
create.ponder.track_portal.text_3: Trains running on it can now cross over into another dimension
create.ponder.track_chunks.text_1: Tracks keep working even where no chunks are loaded
create.ponder.track_chunks.text_2: Trains move through the inactive parts of the world without any trouble
create.ponder.track_chunks.text_3: They still halt at stations and at red signals along the way
create.ponder.track_chunks.text_4: Drills and other machines carried on board, however, stay idle there
create.ponder.track_chunks.text_5: As soon as a player comes close, the train shows up again
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_1: Click a train track first, then place the station beside it
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_2: Stations act as the named stops of your whole railway network
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_3: Open its interface and switch to Assembly Mode to build a new train
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_4: While assembling, trains following a schedule will not come to this station
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_5: Using Train Casing on a track turns that spot into a bogey
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_6: Click the same spot again to switch between the available bogey styles
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_7: Use Super Glue to make the other blocks part of the train
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_8: Fuel found in chests or barrels on board makes the finished train go faster
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_9: Anything kept in an Item Vault is never burned as fuel, though
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_10: Each train needs Train Controls somewhere on board
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_11: A second set facing the other way lets it leave stations in either direction
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_12: Back in the station interface, confirm the assembly to finish the train
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_13: Turning a train back into blocks is only possible at a station
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_14: Using a map on a station puts a named marker for it on the map
create.ponder.train_assembly.text_15: With a Wrench, an assembled train can be moved onto tracks close by
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_1: A schedule tells the driver of a train where to go
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_2: A comparator reading the station outputs a signal while a train is there
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_3: Keep in mind that trains can only pull in from the direction the station points to
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_4: A station can also hand out new schedules to trains by itself
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_5: Any train stopping there gets a copy of the schedule placed on the station
create.ponder.auto_schedule.text_6: Unlike handing it over by hand, the original item stays with the station
create.ponder.train_signal_placement.tex: Click a train track, then put the signal down next to it
Signals direct the traffic of every train that is not steered by a player
Trains on a schedule never pass a signal from its back side
...that changes once a second signal facing the other way is added
Nixie tubes placed on a signal make its light easier to see
create.ponder.train_signal_signaling.tex: Signals cut a track up into separate segments
While one train occupies a segment, no other train may enter it
This way, every segment only ever holds a single train
A Wrench switches a signal to its second mode
A segment starting at a brass signal usually ends at regular signals
This kind of signal can hold trains back for one more reason
It keeps out any train that, after entering...
...could not get out of the segment again right away
That way, waiting trains queue up outside a busy segment instead of blocking it
create.ponder.train_signal_redstone.head: Signals & Redstone
create.ponder.train_signal_redstone.text: Powering a signal with redstone forces it to show red
The other way round, a red signal gives out a comparator signal
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_1: Schedules let trains be driven by someone other than you
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_2: Right-click with it in your hand to open its interface
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_3: When it is set up, give the schedule to a train driver
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_4: Any mob or blaze burner seated right in front of the Train Controls can drive
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_5: Mobs on a lead can be put into their seat more easily
create.ponder.train_schedule.text_6: You can take a schedule back from its driver whenever you like
create.ponder.train_controls.text_1: Every train contraption must carry Train Controls
create.ponder.train_controls.text_2: After assembly, right-click them to take the wheel
create.ponder.train_controls.text_3: Use your movement keys to speed up, slow down and pick a direction at junctions
create.ponder.train_controls.text_4: Scroll the mouse wheel to adjust the top speed if you like
create.ponder.train_controls.text_5: Hold space to bring the train in to a station nearby
create.ponder.train_controls.text_6: Trains can only be broken back down into blocks at a station
create.ponder.train_controls.text_7: Press the sprint key to sound any whistles built into the train
create.ponder.train_controls.text_8: Sneak, or click the controls once more, to let go of the train
create.ponder.track_observer.text_1: Click a train track, then place the observer close to it
create.ponder.track_observer.text_2: The observer reacts to every train that rolls over its marker
create.ponder.track_observer.text_3: A filter limits the observer to trains carrying matching cargo
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.header: Relaying rotational force using Chain Conveyors
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.text_1: Right-click two conveyors while holding chains to link them together
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.text_2: Linked chain conveyors pass rotation on to one another..
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.text_3: ..and they also hook up to shafts directly above or below
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.text_4: Right-click a chain with a wrench in hand to ride along it
create.ponder.chain_conveyor.text_5: Where several chains meet, look at the one you want to take next
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_1: Click a chain conveyor with the frogport, then put it down nearby
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_3: Give it an address in its inventory screen
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_4: Whenever an inserted package carries an address it does not match..
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_6: ..the frogport hands it over to the chain conveyor
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_7: A package with nowhere to go just keeps spinning on the spot
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_8: Further frogports can sit anywhere along the chain network
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_10: Each package travels the network until it reaches the frog with its address
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_11: A frogport moves items straight into the inventory underneath it
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_12: Packagers work with it too: items get boxed up and sent off in a single step
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_13: Right-click a frogport with a clipboard to note down its address
create.ponder.package_frogport.text_14: Addresses noted on a clipboard are suggested when typing addresses in other screens
create.ponder.postbox.text_1: Click a train station with the postbox, then set it down nearby
create.ponder.postbox.text_3: Give it an address in its inventory screen
create.ponder.postbox.text_4: When a package placed inside is meant for another address..
create.ponder.postbox.text_6: ..trains that stop at the station pick it up as cargo
create.ponder.postbox.text_7: In turn, packages carrying this postbox's address are unloaded into it
create.ponder.postbox.text_9: Packages delivered by train can be pulled out of the postbox
create.ponder.postbox.text_10: Postboxes, like trains, keep doing their job in unloaded chunks
create.ponder.postbox.text_11: Packages are still picked up from and dropped into their inventory
create.ponder.packager.text_1: Place packagers against the inventory they should work on
create.ponder.packager.text_2: A redstone signal makes it box up items from the inventory into a package
create.ponder.packager.text_3: Packages can be picked up and moved around like any other item
create.ponder.packager.text_4: A package put into the packager is opened, and its contents go into the inventory
create.ponder.packager.text_6: Packagers refuse any package they could not unpack completely
create.ponder.packager_address.text_2: Once a sign is attached to a packager..
create.ponder.packager_address.text_4: ..every package it makes carries the sign's text as its address
create.ponder.packager_address.text_5: Package filters send packages on depending on their address
create.ponder.packager_address.text_10: To save space, a mechanical saw can cut packages open right onto a belt
create.ponder.packager_address.text_11: Besides filters, frogports and postboxes can also route packages
create.ponder.packager_address.text_12: Look them up to learn more about how they behave
create.ponder.stock_link.header: Logistics Networks and the Stock Link
create.ponder.stock_link.text_1: Placing a Stock Link starts a new stock network
create.ponder.stock_link.text_2: Click an existing link with the new one before placing it to join the two
create.ponder.stock_link.text_3: Packagers with a link share the contents of their inventory with the network
create.ponder.stock_link.text_4: Other parts of the network can then see and order those items
create.ponder.stock_link.text_5: When something is requested, the items are packed up from those inventories
create.ponder.stock_link.text_6: Link signals reach any distance, but the packages still need a way to travel
create.ponder.stock_link.text_7: A full-strength redstone signal stops a link from broadcasting
create.ponder.stock_link.text_8: Weaker signals lower its priority, so other links get to act first
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_1: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_2: Linked packagers offer the items in their inventory to the network
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_3: From a stock ticker, items can be ordered out of those inventories
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_4: A seated mob or a blaze burner in front of it serves as the Stock Keeper
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_5: Right-click the keeper to begin ordering
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_6: Once the order is sent, the items get packed into packages
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_7: From there they still have to be brought to where they were ordered
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_8: Attribute or list filters can sort the listed items into categories
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_9: Right-click the stock ticker itself to edit those categories
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_10: Stock tickers can also order the blocks a schematicannon needs
create.ponder.stock_ticker.text_11: Just give the clipboard printed by the cannon to the Stock Keeper
create.ponder.stock_ticker_address.text_: An order can be given a destination address when it is placed
Every package made for that order is labelled with this address
Package filters then decide where each of those packages ends up
Besides filters, frogports and postboxes can also route packages
Look them up to learn more about how they behave
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_1: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_2: Like stock tickers, redstone requesters order items from the network
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_3: Right-click the requester to set up its order
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_4: Each redstone pulse sends out the order configured there
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_5: You can also set a requester up completely before placing it
create.ponder.redstone_requester.text_6: Right-click a Stock Keeper with it and pick the order there
create.ponder.repackager.text_1: Some requests only work if everything shows up in a single package
create.ponder.repackager.text_5: If not, packages from other orders may slip in between the pieces
create.ponder.repackager.text_6: In that case, let the packages run into an inventory first
create.ponder.repackager.text_7: Put a re-packager on it and give it redstone power
create.ponder.repackager.text_9: As soon as every piece has come in, they leave together as one new package
create.ponder.repackager.text_10: Requested items now arrive together, in an order you can rely on
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_1: Table cloths make a neat surface for showing off items
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_2: Combined with a logistics network, they can turn into a shop
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_3: Begin with the shop's storage, a Packager and a Stock Link
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_4: Link a Stock Ticker to it and place it inside the shop
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_5: Hire a mob or a blaze burner as the shopkeeper
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_6: Stock the shop's inventory with whatever is for sale
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_7: To set up a new offer, use a table cloth on the shopkeeper
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_8: Once it is placed, enter a price in the slot on its side
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_9: Now other players can use the shop
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_10: After paying the shopkeeper, the purchased items are boxed up
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_11: From there, they have to be carried to the front of the shop
create.ponder.table_cloth.text_12: The payments collect inside the stock ticker
create.ponder.factory_gauge_restocker.te: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
Mounted on a packager, a factory gauge keeps an eye on the items in its inventory
Right-click it holding the item it should watch
It now displays how many of them the inventory holds
The gauge can top up this inventory using the logistics network
Right-click it once more to open its settings
Choose the address the requested items should be sent to
Hold right-click on the gauge to set the amount it should keep in stock
Every time the chest drops below that amount...
...the network ships more of it, labelled with the chosen address
From there, send the packages on into the gauge's packager
create.ponder.factory_gauge_recipe.text_: When a gauge is placed anywhere other than on a packager...
...it watches the stock of every inventory linked to the network instead
Right-click it holding the item it should watch
It now displays the total number found across the network
The gauge can keep that number up by sending other items off to be processed
First, put down a new factory gauge for each ingredient
New connections are made from the target gauge's settings
For looks, a Wrench on an input panel changes the route of its connection
The screen lists the inputs; set how many outputs each batch produces
Pick the address the ingredients should be delivered to
Hold right-click on the gauge to set the amount to keep in stock
Whenever the network holds less than that amount...
...a new batch of ingredients goes out to the chosen address
The products then have to find their way back into a linked inventory
Connections turn green once the target amount has been reached
Add more gauges to the board to cover further steps of a recipe
Every gauge looks after the stock of its own item on its own
create.ponder.factory_gauge_crafting.tex: Factory gauges can lay out crafting table recipes for you
Connect the needed ingredients the same way as before
When the gauge recognises a valid recipe, an extra button shows up in its screen
With that turned on, packages can be unpacked right into the crafters
The crafters must form a 3x3 grid and be joined together with a Wrench
Hold right-click on the gauge to choose the target amount
The same crafters can now serve other gauges with different recipes too
Send the results back to a linked inventory to complete the cycle
A Re-packager is a good idea so the incoming packages are not split up
create.ponder.factory_gauge_links.text_1: When you add a new connection in the gauge's screen...
create.ponder.factory_gauge_links.text_2: ...redstone links and display links can be picked as well
create.ponder.factory_gauge_links.text_3: A redstone link is powered while the stock is at or above the target amount
create.ponder.factory_gauge_links.text_4: Set to receive, a link can hold the gauge back from sending requests
create.ponder.factory_gauge_links.text_5: Display links can show an overview of the gauges they are connected to
